ui.installAsk: Install FlussoLab as an app? It also works offline.
ui.installHow:
FlussoLab installs like an app and then works without internet too.

  • Chrome or Edge (Windows, Chromebook, Android): browser menu → “Install FlussoLab” or “Add to Home screen”.
  • iPhone and iPad: open the site in Safari, tap Share → “Add to Home Screen”.

guide:
How to use it

  • Tap a + on a line to insert a block there. OUT writes and stays on the line, OUTLN writes and starts a new line.
  • Explain shows next to each block what it does. Options has the ≥ ≤ ≠ symbols and light or dark theme.
  • Tap a block to edit it in the Block panel. Blocks with an error have a dashed red border.
  • Run starts the program. Step runs one block at a time and shows the variables.
  • Save creates a .flusso file to hand in. File → Export submission (ZIP) puts all open diagrams in one file, as .flusso and as images. Open loads it back. Image exports the diagram as PNG.
  • Right-click a block and choose Disable to skip it when running: handy for OUT blocks used only to check values, before checking an exercise.
  • File → Create exercise: write the task and some tests (input and expected output), then share the link. Students press Check in the Exercise tab and see which tests pass.
  • File → Share link creates a link with the whole diagram inside: whoever opens it gets a copy. Nothing is uploaded to a server.
  • Your work stays saved in this browser even if you close the page.

Expressions

+ − *arithmetic; between two texts, + joins them: "Hi " + name, for a number use str(n)
/division, as in C: between two int the result is an int (7 / 2 → 3); if one is float the result is float (7.0 / 2 → 3.5)
(float) (int)type cast: (float) s / n → division with decimals; (int) 3.9 → 3
mod %remainder: 7 mod 3 and 7 % 3 are the same
^power
== !=equal, not equal. A single = is only for assignment
< <= > >=comparisons
AND OR NOTalso && || !
true, falseboolean values
v[i]array element; created by assigning v[0] = 5 or reading v[i]
i++ i--in the assignment block: adds or subtracts 1 from an integer variable

Variable types

By default the type is automatic: the value decides it. You can declare it where the variable is born, for example IN int n, float avg = (float) s / n or FOR int i = 1 TO 10, or with the VAR block. The types are int (whole numbers), float (numbers with decimals, double works too), string (text) and bool (true or false). For an array write v[]. Type words cannot be used as variable names. FlussoLab reports a value of the wrong type; with IN, a string variable keeps the text as typed, even if it is digits.

Functions

sqrt abs int float round floor ceil pow min max sin cos tan random() randint(a,b) len str num

Shortcuts

Del deletes the selected block · Ctrl+Z undo · Ctrl+C/V copy and paste after the selected block

The project

FlussoLab is free and its code is open to everyone, but it cannot be used to make money. It runs entirely in the browser: nothing to install, Chromebooks and tablets included.
